_comment: Tier-2 for kratos.mpm pitfalls #2 and #3: MATERIAL_POINTS_PER_ELEMENT is mandatory, lives in the MATERIALS json (properties[i].Material.Variables, not ProjectParameters), and its value must come from a per-geometry allowed set. Executed 2026-08-07 on Kratos 10.4.3 Release with MPMApplication. The fixture writes its own two-mdpa deck -- a 1x2 column of quadrilateral background-grid cells with one MPMUpdatedLagrangian2D4N body element in the top cell -- so it depends on no data files, and drives MpmAnalysis.Initialize() three times. Measured: value 1 initialises; omitting the key raises RuntimeError 'Error: "MATERIAL_POINTS_PER_ELEMENT" is not specified in Properties' from material_point_generator_utility; value 5 raises 'Error: The input number of MATERIAL_POINTS_PER_ELEMENT (5) is not available for Quadrilateral elements' + 'Available options are: 1, 4, 9, 16 and 25.'. The allowed sets differ per grid geometry and were read back from the installed libKratosMPMCore: Triangular 1/3/4/6/12, Quadrilateral 1/4/9/16/25, Tetrahedral 1/4/8/14/24, Hexahedral 1/8/27/64/125. VERSION SENSITIVITY, stated because it changes the observable: Kratos master after this release downgrades both of these to warnings that silently clamp to the geometry default, so on a newer build the same mistake produces a wrong material-point count instead of an error. This fixture pins the INSTALLED build's behaviour and will need re-verification against a newer wheel. INTERPRETER: needs a Kratos build carrying MPMApplication; set KRATOS_PYTHON. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable): the mutation INVERTS all three expectations -- 1 must fail, omission and 5 must succeed -- leaving the MpmAnalysis invocation untouched. Verified: unmutated PASSES (rc=0) with material_point_count_mismatches=0; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1), the count goes to 3 and all three accepted[...]_expected=... lines flip. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/mpm_material_points_per_element_is_required && $KRATOS_PYTHON source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 $KRATOS_PYTHON source.py (fails). FIXED 2026-08-08 (forbid changed): forbid_in_output was 'MISMATCH', matched by the runner as a plain case-insensitive substring -- and this fixture's own SUCCESS line is '{key}=0', which contains 'mismatch'. The tripwire therefore fired on the line that says nothing went wrong, so the fixture was red on every run whatever Kratos did, and the red carried no information. The needle is now 'MISMATCH: ' with the colon, which only the per-case failure print emits. PROVEN BY EXECUTION 2026-08-08 on Kratos 10.4.3 with KRATOS_PYTHON=/mnt/kratos-tier2/kv/bin/python, through scripts/run_tier2_fixtures.py --fixture: unmutated PASSES; T2_MUTATE=1 emits 'MISMATCH: ' lines and a non-zero count, rc=1. Before the change the runner reported "forbidden tokens appeared: ['MISMATCH']" on the unmutated run. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS (source changed): with the tripwire corrected the fixture was still red, and the reason was a buffer boundary rather than anything Kratos did. Kratos prints its banners from C++ with a block-buffered stdout; at byte 4096 of the captured stream a DEPRECATION-Warning line was cut mid-word and the fixture's own next line was glued to it ('...ModifyAfterSolverInitiaaccepted[mpp=1]=True_expected=True'). The runner rejects a key=value needle whose preceding character is alphanumeric -- correctly, that guard is what stops one expectation matching a longer key -- so the expectation went missing. The assertion lines now carry a leading newline inside the same write. Measured 2026-08-08: before, "missing in output: ['accepted[mpp=1]=True_expected=True']" at index 4096; after, the runner reports passed, and T2_MUTATE=1 still reports rc=1 with the count at 3.
expect_in_output: is not available for Quadrilateral elements
